[MUQATIL:23:1-6/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Doing zakah means paying the zakah due on their wealth.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p393/r3] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | They perform the obligatory alms payment.
[ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r1] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | فاعلون means those who give zakat.
[NAHHAS:v3p109/r6] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | God praises even those who give only the zakāt due from their wealth; hoarders of gold and silver are those who fail to pay zakāt.
[KHATTABI:v1p37/r7] KHATTABI, d. 388 · author | reports | An objection says that Arabic does not say someone ‘does zakāh’; it uses verbs such as give, pay, or purify one’s wealth.
[KHATTABI:v1p44/r7] KHATTABI, d. 388 · author | prefers | ‘Doers of zakāh’ conveys sustained, habitual performance as a defining trait, whereas ordinary verbs merely report that payment occurred; this is the most complete and forceful wording.
[KHATTABI:v1p44/r8] KHATTABI, d. 388 · قيل | reports | Another view takes zakāh here as righteous work and virtuous deeds, so the phrase means that they perform good and pure actions.
[THALABI:v7p39/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The believers perform and pay the obligatory zakat.
[THALABI:v7p39/r7] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The expression is good Arabic usage; Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt’s verse likewise speaks of paying zakat.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r11] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Zakat means growth, but spiritual growth requires diminishing one’s own self-witness; complete servitude comes only by dissolving that witness.
[WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1] WAHIDI-ASBAB, d. 468 · عمر بن الخطاب | reports | Umar describes revelation’s bee-like sound and the Prophet’s supplication, then reports that whoever upholds the first ten verses of al-Muʾminun enters Paradise.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says they give zakat from their wealth seeking God’s pleasure.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الكلبي | reports | Al-Kalbi says they fulfill the obligatory charity.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أبو إسحاق | reports | Abu Ishaq explains فاعلون as مؤتون, “giving.”
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r4] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Being active in zakat means paying the obligatory alms.
[JISHUMI:v7p5024/r11] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Zakat is obligatory and a condition of faith, subject to conditions such as ownership of the minimum amount for a full year.
[JISHUMI:v7p5024/r12] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Zakat is a legally prescribed act of worship.
[JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | No other required duties are omitted: worship, contracts, and liabilities fall under trusts and covenants; sins fall under avoiding laghw.
[JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The listed traits remove ambiguity: whoever has them is a believer, supporting the author’s position.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p409#2/r5] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The phrase means that believers pay the obligatory zakat; it calls payment an action because payment is itself an act.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p409#2/r6] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · قيل | reports | An alternate interpretation takes zakat here to mean righteous deeds.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r12] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الطبري وغيره | reports | Al-Ṭabarī and others take zakāh here to mean the obligatory alms due on wealth; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this clear.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r13] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | The wording could also mean pursuing virtues, taking the best or purest course in every action, as in 18:81. | mentions 18:81
[TABRISI:23:4-10/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The phrase means they pay alms; payment is called doing because it is an act, with Umayya’s line cited as evidence.
[TABRISI:23:4-10/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas specifies that they perform the obligatory alms.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p460#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | They perform zakat; the verse uses the general word doing because payment is an act.
[QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r13] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The author says the meanings of idle talk and zakat were already discussed in al-Baqara and need not be repeated. | mentions 2:219
[QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r17] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Fāʿilūn means those who perform or pay it; this usage is eloquent and attested in Arab speech, including poetry by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:23:4/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Following bodily worship with financial worship shows they reach the utmost in religious duties and avoidance of forbidden and unbecoming things. | mentions 23:2
[BAYDAWI-FULL:23:4/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | Zakāt may denote the abstract duty, since an agent performs the event rather than its object; or the material after ellipsis of a genitive noun.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | They perform zakat, and the wording “doers” suggests continuing practice more clearly than “payers.”
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Zakat can mean the payment itself or the act of purification; the latter is intended, with the performers named for doing it.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Alternatively, zakat means the payment, with “performance” omitted; the preceding object takes a lām because the active participle has weaker verbal force.
[QASHANI:23:1-11/r4] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | Their zakat is detachment from their own traits.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أمية بن أبي الصلت | reports | The poet's plural الزكوات is cited as sound Arabic evidence for the expression; Arab eloquence scholars accepted and cited it.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī prefers reading the poem's plural as referring to the paid amounts, with an omitted word for their performance.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | When an active participle's object precedes it, the lām may strengthen its transitivity as with a verb; the same is possible after it, though fronting is commoner, and accusative would also be Arabic.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | If zakāh means purification, the action can be attributed to it; if it means the payment, the phrase elides its performance or uses fāʿilūn to mean those who deliver it, as al-Tabrīzī explains.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو مسلم | reports | Zakah here can mean righteous action, as in the phrase describing something better in zakāh. | mentions 18:81
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قيل | reports | Zakah can mean growth and increase; the lām is causal, with the implied sense that they do good to obtain increase.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قيل | reports | Some hold that wealth is not called zakāh until it reaches the poor recipient.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Some say the paid object itself is not called zakāh, making the verbal form more apt; the author rejects a foreign skeptic's demand for مؤدون as unsupported by reason or transmission and defends the Qur'an's eloquent Arabic.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p548/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | The author rejects the preceding argument that zakāh must mean the paid object because verbal nouns cannot be pluralized: plural verbal nouns exist, and zakāh varies by type of payment.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p548/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | The author rejects the claim that verbal nouns cannot be plural: plural examples exist, and zakāh can vary with the kind of money or produce being paid.
[SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The lām is an added marker on the object because it precedes its governing verb and is a derived noun.
[SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Zakat is originally a verbal noun and also denotes the amount taken from taxable property.
[SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari says zakat can name either the paid amount or the act of giving it; here the intended sense is the act, which its performers can do.
[SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari argues that فاعلون properly attaches to the verbal noun, since an agent is said to perform the act, as in performing a blow or killing.
[SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari also allows zakat to mean the amount paid, with an omitted word الأداء; he reads Umayya's plural poem this way because the source noun is not pluralized.
[SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أمية بن أبي الصلت | reports | Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's line uses the plural الزكوات; al-Zamakhshari takes it as referring to amounts of zakat rather than the verbal noun.
[SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The author explains that al-Zamakhshari answers those who thought the concrete sense impossible with فاعلون: it is not impossible by grammar, but people do not produce the zakat amounts.
[SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | reports | The Shaykh objects that zakat may still be a verbal noun here and pluralized because its kinds differ.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | prefers | Most commentators take zakah here as wealth alms despite the sura being Meccan; the fixed thresholds were prescribed in Medina in year two, while the basic duty likely began in Mecca, as 6:141 indicates. | mentions 6:141
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | reports | Another possible meaning is purification of the soul from shirk and impurity, as in the verses about one who purifies the self and those who do not give zakah, on one interpretation. | mentions 91:9, 91:10, 4

[ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الراغب | reports | Al-Rāghib chooses the sense purity, with the lām expressing purpose: they perform worship so God may purify them or they may purify themselves.

[ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعض الأجلة | reports | An eminent scholar argues that pairing this trait with prayer signals the financial worship of paying zakāt; the comparison to the purification verses is remote.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | A further argument for al-Rāghib's non-legal reading is that the sūra is Meccan while zakāt became obligatory in Medina, avoiding the need for earlier interpretive adjustments.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | rejects | Al-Ālūsī ridicules a non-Arab critic's claim that مؤدون would be better than فاعلون, arguing that the Prophet's eloquence was unmatched and hostile Arab critics would have seized on any real flaw.

[ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The apparent sense of zakāt is the verbal noun tazkiya, since an action applies to the process; if it means the payment itself, an implied word for performing it is needed.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · التبريزي | reports | Al-Tabrīzī explains the phrase as performing the payment of zakāt, either by supplying أداء or taking فاعلون to mean payers; the latter is criticized because Arabic does not idiomatically say فعلت الزكاة for paying it.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | If zakāt means purification, describing them as doing tazkiya entails the actual payment by metonymy, a more eloquent way to express it and one reason for this wording over والذين يزكون.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Several earlier explanations for the greater eloquence of turning away from idle talk rather than merely not engaging in it also apply here; the fronted object may focus information rather than restrict meaning, or imply contrast with improper spending.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Positioning zakāt after prayer depicts full effort in bodily and financial worship; placing avoidance of idle talk between them links closely to prayer, though the Qurʾān often mentions the two duties together.
[ELMALILI:23:3-8/r2] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | The immediate sense of doing zakat is giving zakat from one's wealth.
[ELMALILI:23:3-8/r3] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · bazıları | reports | Some understand zakat here to mean refinement and purification.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Here zakah denotes the money given, using the verbal noun for its resulting object; the construction with doers requires an object, as in the command to take charity that purifies. | mentions 9:103

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The implied action is giving zakah, equivalent to they give zakah; there is no need to supply a separate word for performance. | mentions 5:55

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · أمية بن أبي الصلت | reports | A poem attributed to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt uses zakah for charitable giving, but Ibn Ashur doubts its attribution because this sense may derive from Qur'anic terminology.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · ابن قتيبة | reports | Ibn Qutayba says scholars do not treat Umayya's poetry as authoritative evidence against the Qur'an.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | On Ibn Ashur's reading of zakah as the object of doers, lam reinforces a weak derived verb that follows its object.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · الكشاف | reports | Al-Kashshaf calls zakah a verbal noun meaning the giver's act of giving zakah and says doer naturally takes such a verbal-noun complement.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | rejects | Ibn Ashur says al-Kashshaf privileges formal grammar to explain the construction, and its analysis depends on an unnecessary implied noun or verbal-noun reading.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Prayer and zakah frequently occur together in Qur'an; here avoiding frivolity separates them for a thematic reason discussed earlier.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Giving zakah is proper conduct toward people in need and belongs to ethics governing the use of wealth.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The repeated relative pronoun and fronting of the object follow the same construction explained for the preceding qualities.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Zakah here means charity, not the later fixed levy on specified wealth, so its mention does not date the sura to Medina.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The Qur'an uses zakah for charity in Meccan Fussilat, and says Isma'il commanded his household to pray and give zakah before the fixed levy existed. | mentions 41:6, 41:7, 19:54, 19:55
